what: Remote ID: the broadcast most US drones must send about themselves (ASTM F3411, FAA Part 89). A drone-like signal with no Remote ID is a reason to look closer; it is not proof of anything, because homebuilt and older drones may be exempt or non-compliant, and Remote ID can be spoofed.
source: Open Drone ID project (https://github.com/opendroneid), opendroneid-core-c libopendroneid/opendroneid.h; ASTM F3411

transports.name: Bluetooth 5 long range (coded PHY)
transports.note: Secondary channels can be anywhere in 2402-2480 MHz

transports.name: Wi-Fi Neighbor Awareness (NaN)
transports.note: Channel 6 at 2.4 GHz, channel 149 at 5 GHz

transports.name: Wi-Fi beacon
transports.note: Any Wi-Fi channel the drone uses

message_types.0: Basic ID: serial number or registration ID
message_types.1: Location: drone position, altitude, speed, heading
message_types.3: Self-ID: free-text description of the flight
message_types.4: System: operator (pilot) location and area of operation
